topic: Sanctions, exports and shadow-fleet operations (2025-2026 update)
wiki_text: [CONFIRMED] Despite full US/EU sanctions on the project, its operating company and associated LNG carriers, Arctic LNG 2 resumed and steadily expanded LNG exports through 2025-2026 using a 'shadow fleet' of older, sanctions-exposed carriers. After Train 1 was idled in spring 2025 (storage full for lack of ice-class tankers), satellite data showed production resuming end-March 2025; by September 2025 the plant hit record output (~18 million cubic metres of gas liquefaction per day, ~14% above its prior record) and had shipped multiple cargoes to China (e.g. to the Beihai LNG terminal). Cargoes are moved via giant floating storage units (FSUs) Saam (near Murmansk) and Koryak (Kamchatka) at the ends of the Northern Sea Route, with the ice-class carrier Christophe de Margerie shuttling between the Utrenny terminal and the Saam FSU. Analysts estimate the plant runs at roughly 30% of nameplate, constrained chiefly by a shortage of ice-class LNG carriers rather than liquefaction capacity; Train 1 itself is reported to run at ~50% capacity after sanctions deprived the project of 3 of 7 Baker Hughes LM9000 turbines. The EU's planned full ban on Russian LNG imports from 1 January 2027 is driving Novatek to expand a parallel export fleet.

[UNVERIFIED - SINGLE SOURCE] Construction of Train 3 (the third gravity-based-structure liquefaction line) largely stalled in 2024 under sanctions. In April 2026 the first known Train-3 components since the halt - two pipe-rack modules (3-TMR-001 and 3-TMR-002) - departed China for Russia, and Novatek was reported to plan towing the final GBS line from the Belokamenka construction yard near Murmansk to the Gydan peninsula around July 2026. Train 3 start-up had previously been postponed to 2028 (from 2026). There is reported uncertainty over whether the third line's equipment will be used to complete Arctic LNG 2 Train 3 or instead be redirected to Novatek's Murmansk LNG project.

[UNVERIFIED - SINGLE SOURCE] US sanctions taking full effect on 27 February 2025 hit both the Portovaya LNG facility and its associated LNG carriers, leading to a suspension of international LNG shipments from the terminal as of mid-2025. The plant's two operating trains (~1.5 mtpa combined) remain physically operable. Plans announced in September 2022 for a third liquefaction train (~2 mtpa, domestic technology) have seen no further updates and the expansion is treated as shelved.

[CONFLICTING DATA] In January 2025 Novatek reportedly reduced the planned Murmansk LNG capacity to about 13.6 Mt/year (implying two ~6.8 mtpa trains rather than three) and pulled the completion date forward to 2030 (from 2033), with a loading ramp of ~3.4 Mt in 2028, ~6.8 Mt in 2029 and ~13.6 Mt from 2030. The plant would be fed by a new ~1,300 km Volkhov-Murmansk gas pipeline (up to ~41.2 bcm/y). However, Russia's Energy Strategy to 2050 (April 2025) lists Murmansk LNG total capacity at 20.4 mtpa (the three-train figure GEM currently models). Novatek had suspended work on the Murmansk and Ob LNG projects in September 2024 under sanctions before the project was re-prioritised in early 2025. Sources thus conflict on whether the project is 13.6 mtpa (2 trains) or 20.4 mtpa (3 trains).

topic: ExxonMobil Sakhalin-1 stake — status after January 2026 deadline
wiki_text: [CONFIRMED] ExxonMobil's roughly 30% stake in the underlying Sakhalin-1 project (which feeds the proposed Far East LNG plant at De Kastri) was effectively seized by a Russian decree in October 2022 that transferred operatorship to Rosneft subsidiary Sakhalinmorneftegaz-Shelf. Russia granted Exxon successive extensions to divest, most recently to 1 January 2026. In September 2025 ExxonMobil and Rosneft reached a non-binding agreement intended to help Exxon recoup losses and potentially return to the project, explicitly conditioned on a Russia-Ukraine peace settlement and an easing of US/EU sanctions - neither of which had occurred as of mid-2026. As of this update no new equity holder for the 30% had been confirmed, and the project remained proposed/pre-FID. India's ONGC Videsh (~20%) and Japan's SODECO consortium retained their stakes.
